# Regex fixtures for skill: second-opinion
# Format: one directive per non-empty, non-comment line.
#   MATCH: <prompt>     — regex from config/default-triggers.json for this skill must match
#   NO_MATCH: <prompt>  — regex must NOT match
# Tested deterministically by tests/test-regex-fixtures.sh (zero LLM cost).
#
# Contract C1: ONE other model's view. Two modes — independent opinion (prior answer
# withheld) and critique (prior answer deliberately included).
#
# EVERY NO_MATCH below was MEASURED selecting this skill in a first attempt that was
# reverted, and each one is a real cost, not a style point: this skill performs a
# cross-family dispatch, so a false match proposes shipping repository content to another
# vendor. See openspec/changes/composition-contract-fixes/C1-RETRY.md.
#
# The first three NO_MATCH lines are verbatim-borrowed from panel.txt's and
# design-debate's MATCH sets, pinning the three-way boundary from the other side.

# WHY THESE CLAUSES KEEP A TRAILING ($|[^a-z]) AND PANEL'S MULTI CLAUSE DOES NOT.
# The scorer grades a match 30 only when BOTH edges sit on a word boundary; a trailing
# group consumes the delimiter, so the right edge lands mid-word and the clause scores
# 10. That cost panel its own multi-model prompt (28 vs 47) and panel's clause therefore
# ends ON the participant.
#
# These clauses keep the group deliberately, and the trade is the other way round: it is
# what rejects `ask codexfoo to do it` and `consult geminid about the schema`. Dropping
# it would let a partial word route to an OUTBOUND cross-vendor dispatch, which is the
# severe direction; scoring 10 only affects ranking. Measured: second-opinion still takes
# domain slot 1/2 on every contested prompt tried, including against incident-analysis at
# 50. If a future competitor does displace it, fix the CONTEST (priority, or a more
# specific clause) -- do not drop the boundary group.

MATCH: get a second opinion from another model on this migration plan
MATCH: ask codex to weigh in on this approach
MATCH: consult codex about the schema change
MATCH: here is my answer - have codex critique it
MATCH: what does codex think of the proposed fix
MATCH: run this by codex
MATCH: send this to gemini for a second look
MATCH: double-check my conclusion with a second model
MATCH: i want an independent read from one other model before i commit
MATCH: have another model critique the answer you just gave

NO_MATCH: run a panel of models on this design
NO_MATCH: give me a model panel on these two options
NO_MATCH: let's debate the tradeoffs between a monolith and microservices architecture
# NOT asserted here: "ask codex, gemini and gpt-5 each for their take" DOES match
# this trigger. ERE has no lookahead, so the pattern cannot reject a participant LIST.
# Panel outranks it (49 vs 47) and takes slot 1 -- a routing outcome no regex fixture
# can express, asserted against the real hook in tests/test-second-opinion-content.sh.
#
# An earlier version of this comment justified the omission with "priority 18 vs 17 at
# equal match count". That was measurably FALSE: match count was 2 vs 1, and panel's
# clause scored 10 rather than 30 because it consumed the delimiters on both sides, so
# panel actually LOST 77 to 28 and was one competing skill away from eviction. The
# repair was match QUALITY (ending panel's clause on the participant so its right edge
# is a word boundary), not the priority number. A comment asserting a scoring outcome
# is a claim; measure it before writing it.
NO_MATCH: please critique my approach to caching
NO_MATCH: sanity check the deployment plan
NO_MATCH: poke holes in my plan for the migration
NO_MATCH: tear apart the design doc i wrote
NO_MATCH: grade my answer to the interview question
NO_MATCH: red team the rollout plan with the infra team
NO_MATCH: let's use a different model for the pricing table
NO_MATCH: we should train another model on the new dataset
NO_MATCH: there is no other model of concurrency that fits
NO_MATCH: swap in an independent model for the risk score
NO_MATCH: get a second opinion on our threat model
NO_MATCH: add a task codex entry to the backlog
NO_MATCH: we need to get codex installed on this machine
NO_MATCH: get a second opinion from the reviewer before merging
NO_MATCH: please review my opinion on the caching strategy
NO_MATCH: add an independent perspectives section to the report
# Gap expressions stop at ; and : as well as . ! ? -- otherwise they bridge separate
# statements into an apparent consultation. NOTE: the class is [^.!?;:] and must NOT
# gain a \n escape: a bash ERE bracket expression does not interpret it, so [^.!?;:\n]
# excludes the LETTER n and no gap can span a word like "conclusion".
NO_MATCH: we swapped in a different model; unrelated: send the critique to the team
MATCH: double-check my conclusion with a second model

# ROUND-4 PHRASING GAPS (measured 2026-09-16, held-out set, then SPENT by inspection).
# All five name a vendor and still failed to route -- the lists were right but the
# grammar was not: English separates particle verbs ("tear IT apart" vs the listed
# "tear apart"), and "second PAIR of eyes" is as common as "set of eyes". Fixing these
# required NO weakening of the AI-participant requirement, which is why it was safe.
MATCH: take my original question to o3 clean, no priming, no mention of your answer
MATCH: second pair of eyes from gpt-5 on the retry design pls
MATCH: paste what you just wrote into o3 and have it tear it apart
MATCH: show gemini your proposed migration plan and ask where it breaks
MATCH: i want gpt-5 to review your answer above, specifically the bit about idempotency keys

# VENDOR-AS-SUBJECT boundary. These name a vendor too, and must stay silent: the vendor
# is the OBJECT OF WORK, not the recipient of a question. A veto clause was designed for
# this and then DROPPED as unnecessary -- clause structure alone keeps them silent, and
# ERE has no negative lookahead, so the veto was unimplementable as a trigger anyway.
NO_MATCH: our openai bill tripled last month, can you dig through the usage logs and figure out why
NO_MATCH: we're migrating off the gemini api to a self hosted llama, write the adapter layer

NO_MATCH: stand up an eval harness that scores our prompt templates against the gpt-4o endpoint
NO_MATCH: what do you actually think of this design, be honest
NO_MATCH: critique my pr description, it's too long and i think the argument is weak
NO_MATCH: argue the other side for me. i think we should keep the monolith, tell me why i'm wrong
